toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

The task sits in /home/sam/.orc/runs/20261110-214051-c18064/session/task.md. Read that file and implement what it asks. When the work is committed on this branch, print ORC_COMPLETE on its own line and stop.

# orc's help is one unreadable line, so a person cannot find a command or learn what it does from `orc --help`.

The captain's words: "current orc help has very bad UX, its not help, add task to make more human friendly help".

Today `orc --help`, `orc backlog --help`, `orc runs --help` and a bare `orc` all print the same single `Usage:` line of about 1,400 characters that chains every command with ` | ` (`usage` in `packages/run/src/bin.ts:21` joined with `dispatchUsage`). A wrong command prints a one-line error followed by that whole line again (`bin.ts:167`). Nothing says what a command does, and a subcommand's `--help` does not narrow to that subcommand.

Make the help read like help:

- `orc --help` and a bare `orc` print a short overview: one line saying what orc is, then the commands grouped by what a person is doing (run a task, the backlog and beat, runs and their results, the runner, chat), each with a one-line plain description, and a closing line pointing at `orc <command> --help`.
- `orc <command> --help` (and `orc backlog <subcommand> --help`, `orc runner <subcommand> --help`) prints only that command: its usage, a sentence or two on what it does, each option with what it means and its accepted values, and one or two realistic examples.
- A wrong or incomplete command prints the specific error and the usage of the nearest command only, plus the pointer to `--help`, not the whole list. An unknown command suggests the closest real one when there is a clear match.
- Lines wrap to fit an 80-column terminal. Exit codes stay as they are: help on stdout with 0, usage errors on stderr with the current non-zero code.
- Keep one source for each command's syntax, so the help, the parser's errors and any future command cannot drift apart; a new subcommand added later must not be able to skip its help entry.

Tests (`tests/e2e/bin.test.ts` already checks `Usage: orc` on stdout and stderr): one case each for the overview listing every top-level command, each command's own `--help` naming only that command, a wrong subcommand printing only its own usage, and every command the parser accepts having a help entry. Name each test for the wrong output it rejects. Update the README and `docs/` pages that quote the old usage line.

## Review findings to address

An earlier run's review raised three points; settle each:

- **Syntax drift between help and parsers.** Do not redesign the parsers into one declarative flag spec. Make drift fail a check instead: a test that every flag and positional each parser accepts (`args.ts` run flags and every flag check in `dispatch/args.ts`) appears in that command's help entry, alongside the existing test for the other direction. Fix the drift it finds today: `runner result` accepts `--stdin-label` but its usage line leaves it out.
- **Overview group slicing.** `formatOverview` builds one wrapped table and slices it into groups by row count, so a summary that wraps shifts every later group. Build the table per group with the shared width: `listed.flatMap((entry) => ["", entry.group, ...table(entry.names.map(commandRow), width)])`. Add a case with a summary long enough to wrap.
- **Overview test oracle.** The overview test takes its expected commands from `commandNames` in the code under test. Compare against the documented literal list instead: run, runs, show, score, chat, backlog, beat, merge, runner.

## Start from the earlier run

An earlier run of this task finished the work in two commits on the branch `orc/task-14` in this checkout. Its checks passed; its review stopped on the three points above.

Before anything else run `git cherry-pick main..orc/task-14` so your branch holds those commits. Read them with `git log -p main..HEAD`, keep what holds, address the three points, and run every check again.


Held for the captain: captain 2026-11-06: no new orc tasks until orc's own problems are fixed; help task starts after them
The captain answered: Yes, go in this order

arguments.command: git status; git log --oneline -3; git log --oneline main..orc/task-14; git cherry-pick main..orc/task-14 && git log --stat main..HEAD
